messages:
Jordan: Quick Q after today's all-hands — when we say 'unified runtime' what fraction of engineering headcount is going to runtime-level work vs. SDK/console/PLG ergonomics over the next 6-12 months?
Lina: Short answer: split roughly 55/45 in favor of runtime for the next two quarters, then shift toward UX and tooling as runtime baseline stabilizes. Runtime gives us cost/latency differentiation now.
Priya: to add: product roadmap sequencing is intentionally hybrid. Q3 focus = runtime perf & predictable batching; Q4 = storefront (deploy/rollout) & evals. We'll publish a one-pager next week.
Tom: engineer note — runtime improvements often unlock cheaper Dedicated options. Also want clarity on when to prioritize quantization support vs. kernel work. Any guidance?
Lina: prioritize kernel work for the most-used model families (Llama, Falcon derivatives) — quantization tooling follows once kernels are stable. That's consistent with 'serve-first' strategy.
Ravi: sales data point: conversations fall into two buckets: 'we need cheaper hosted ops' and 'we need private deployment for compliance.' Competitor X is pushing price-focused messaging; Competitor Y pushes enterprise isolation stories. We should lean into predictable $/token + rollout playbook.
Priya: agreed. We'll craft two collateral tracks: performance benchmarks + Dedicated TCO calculator; compliance checklist + private deployment checklist.
Jordan: can we get a simple chart that maps customer profile -> product recommendation? (startup/prototype -> hosted; scale SaaS -> Dedicated; regulated enterprise -> Private)
Tom: Kevin (ops-bot) can we log a follow-up ticket for the decision matrix?
ops-bot: Follow-up created: #ENG-RT-1234 assigned to Tom, due 2024-11-01. :white_check_mark:
Lina: leadership ask: if any metric on token cost, Dedicated LTV, or hosted conversion moves by >15% in one quarter, we will revisit allocation. We'll share exact thresholds in OKRs.
Jordan: thanks — last ask: how do we measure moat vs. big cloud providers? Is it purely latency/cost or also developer experience?
Priya: moat = combination: reproducible latency/price at scale + integrated rollout/observability that developers trust. That's where we want our story to be unique.
Ravi: will push those bullets into customer decks. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
